subtopics.title: How This Practice Set Is Built

questions.question: Every walked question in this practice set is built on the same staircase, which runs:
options: Paragraph first, then definitions, then sources
Definition, then source-reading, then explanation, then an insight paragraph at the top
Multiple choice from start to finish
Calculations followed by drawing

questions.question: In this practice set, a mark allocation of two marks is an instruction to give:
options: Two separate paragraphs
A labelled diagram
One developed fact
At least half a page of writing

questions.question: The standing rule about blank answers is:
options: Leave a blank when unsure, to save time
Blanks are only allowed on objective items
Blanks earn half marks if the rest is correct
Answer everything, because a blank can never earn a mark and elimination is a legitimate strategy

subtopics.title: The Quick-Fire Warm-Up — Ten Marks Before You Blink

questions.question: The moisture front over the interior separates:
options: Moist eastern air from dry western air
Warm air from cold air along the polar front
Plateau air from coastal air
Summer air from winter air

questions.question: Paired terraces stepping up the sides of a valley are evidence of:
options: River capture
Braiding
Rejuvenation
Delta growth

questions.question: The best way to train warm-up retrieval items is:
options: Rewriting full notes the night before
Daily, aloud and fast, like vocabulary in a language
Reading the textbook once in silence
Practising only the hardest questions

subtopics.title: Walking a Climate Question — Synoptic Chart in Hand

questions.question: Two pieces of map evidence that the described chart shows summer are:
options: Fronts at the Cape and a strong inversion
The subtropical highs lying south of their winter positions and a tropical cyclone existing at all
Widely spaced isobars and a berg wind
A coastal low and winter dates

questions.question: For a two-mark identification like naming the system in the Mozambique Channel, the right answer length is:
options: A full paragraph with examples
A labelled sketch
One precise line, then move on
At least half a page

questions.question: Cyclone Denga poses little direct threat to the Highveld because:
options: Tropical cyclones never cross the coastline
The Highveld is protected by the moisture front
The storm strengthens over land
The storm loses its warm-ocean fuel over land, and distance plus the escarpment leave only decaying rain for the interior

subtopics.title: Walking a Geomorphology Question — River Capture on the Landscape

questions.question: River capture is defined as:
options: The natural diversion of one river's headwaters into a more vigorous neighbouring river by headward erosion
The engineered damming of a river
Two rivers joining at a confluence
A river reaching its graded profile

questions.question: The sharp bend, the dry notch and the shrunken lower course left after capture are, in order:
options: Knickpoint, gorge, delta
Elbow of capture, wind gap, misfit stream
Confluence, watershed, tributary
Meander, terrace, levee

questions.question: River X captured river Y because river X:
options: Was the longer river
Flowed across softer rock everywhere
Fell steeply off the escarpment, giving it greater erosive energy for headward erosion through the watershed
Carried less water

subtopics.title: Walking a Settlement Question — The Emptying Platteland

questions.question: Rural depopulation is:
options: The long-term decline of a rural area's population as people move away, mainly to urban areas
The seasonal migration of harvest workers
The growth of commuter villages around cities
A resettlement scheme run by the state

questions.question: From the Free State extract, which pair are PUSH factors?
options: The solar farm and the tourism route
Bloemfontein's colleges and Gauteng's wages
The sandstone farmsteads and the commonage
Mechanised, consolidated farms shedding work, and the closure of local employers like the mill and co-op

questions.question: In the paragraph task, each of the four ideas earns its second mark by:
options: Being underlined for emphasis
Being developed with an explanation or because-clause in a full sentence
Being repeated in the conclusion
Naming any town

subtopics.title: Walking an Economic Geography Question — Corridors and Sectors

questions.question: An Industrial Development Zone is:
options: A tax on imported machinery
A housing scheme on the urban periphery
A purpose-built industrial estate linked to a port or airport, with serviced sites and incentives for export manufacturing
A conservation corridor between provinces

questions.question: An export factory would choose Coega partly because:
options: The deep-water port alongside cuts the cost and time of shipping to world markets
It stands at the centre of the Highveld
It replaces sea freight with air freight
It is the country's oldest industrial region

questions.question: Gauteng remains the leading industrial region partly because it:
options: Owns the country's only harbour
Faces no competition from coastal regions
Lies closest to world shipping lanes
Grew on the goldfields, holds the largest market and skills pool, and sits at the hub of the national transport network

subtopics.title: The Paragraph Question — Where Insight Becomes Marks

questions.question: The first move of the paragraph recipe is to:
options: Write the conclusion first
Read and obey the instruction verb — suggest, evaluate or discuss
Count the lines on the page
Copy the source material into the answer

questions.question: A paragraph answer written as bullet points:
options: Earns full marks if the facts are right
Earns one bonus mark for neatness
Breaks the paragraph contract — full sentences are compulsory
Is acceptable for the last two ideas only

questions.question: In the model food-security paragraph, 'bank water in good years through farm dams and repaired irrigation' is a strong idea because it:
options: States a workable solution and develops it — stretching supply across dry seasons
Is the shortest of the four ideas
Avoids mentioning water shortages
Repeats the definition of drought
